transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here for the routine project-review meeting on the spring oral-history project. Before we dive in, I'd like to hear from each of you regarding the current draft — specifically the proposed participation by grades 7 and 8, one supervising adult per session, cloud-based audio storage, a 90-day retention period, and the public exhibit of selected recordings. Let's start with any concerns or recommendations from each of your perspectives, and then I'll make a final determination on whether to approve the plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share findings from my classroom pilot. The pilot showed that the project is instructionally ready only for grade 8 — not grade 7. Additionally, each interview session requires exactly two supervising adults, not one, because students are working with recording equipment alongside community guests. I recorded these findings in my end-of-pilot notes, but the current draft plan still contains the original scope and staffing of grades 7–8 and one adult per session.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical discrepancy between the current draft and the privacy review I completed. The district privacy review requires that all recordings remain on the district's encrypted internal server — not cloud-based storage. Additionally, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes, not the 90-day retention period currently in the draft. Finally, signed guardian consent must be obtained before any student records an interview. I completed this review, but the draft still uses the preliminary cloud-storage language and the longer retention period.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share findings from the archive and rights review I completed. The review permits each public exhibit audio excerpt to be no longer than exactly 3 minutes, and it requires contributor attribution beside every excerpt. I completed this rights check, but these limits have not yet been added to the exhibit template that's currently in the draft.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share findings from the family outreach review I completed. Family outreach confirmed that consent materials must be available in exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic, and that paper consent forms must be offered in addition to the online form. I completed this outreach review, but the family-materials checklist has not yet been revised to reflect these requirements.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Update the draft plan to reflect grade 8 only participation and two supervising adults per session, consistent with pilot findings.
Update the draft to specify district encrypted internal server storage, 45-day deletion after exhibit closes, and signed guardian consent before recording.
Update the exhibit template to include the 3-minute maximum excerpt length and contributor attribution beside every excerpt.
Update the family-materials checklist to include consent materials in English, Spanish, and Arabic, with paper consent forms offered in addition to the online form.
All revisions must be completed and submitted for my final sign-off before implementation begins.
